title: I Built a VHS-Style Zombie Dinosaur Survival Roguelite With Codex
author: Worried-Radish-5316
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’ve been developing the concept for a zombie dinosaur survival game with a found-footage/VHS aesthetic.

I created and prepared the dinosaur models, textures, rigs, and animations myself using Blender and Auto-Rig Pro. For the playable prototype, I used Codex and ChatGPT as coding assistants to help me build the gameplay systems in JavaScript and Three.js.

At the same time, it also showed me some important limitations. As the project became larger, performance and code complexity became increasingly difficult to manage. The browser version can struggle on some systems, particularly when loading enemies, animations, or transitioning into QTE sequences.

I’m now considering rebuilding the project in a dedicated engine such as Godot or Unreal Engine. Before starting that process, I would really appreciate feedback from people who have migrated an AI-assisted prototype into a more structured game project.

 I’m also interested in advice about avoiding the same architectural and performance problems during the rebuild.  
  
Playable demo: [ITCH.IO LINK](https://jobbin.itch.io/vhz-1995)

Thank you for taking the time to look at it. Honest and constructive feedback is very welcome.

comments.body:
Very cool trailer. Good job there!  
Gave the game about 10 minutes of testing.  
Here's the issues I ran into, some may be because of browser, some because of build IDK just what happened to me.

\-Spent 4 minutes in first stage unsure what to do or where to go, only by chance did I walk to the next map to actually start playing the game. Need a visual queue of where to go.  
\-Theres a very big lag spike almost every time you shoot right now unsure why.

And thats about it. Did say I only played for 10 minutes haha. But the game is cool, i do think people will buy this if it's given polish personally.

replies.author: Worried-Radish-5316
replies.body:
Hi! Thank you so much for taking the time to play the game and write this feedback! :D

I completely agree with both points. I’ve been investigating the lag spikes, especially the ones that happen when firing. Some of the performance issues may be related to the limitations of running the game in a browser, but I’ll continue optimizing it and adding better graphics settings.

I’ll also improve the beginning of the game by adding a clearer visual indicator showing the player where to go. I really appreciate you mentioning that.

My next major step is to rebuild the game in a dedicated game engine with better performance and more polish. I’ll continue updating the browser version in the meantime.

Thank you again for playing and for giving me such useful feedback. I truly appreciate your time! If you notice anything else, I’ll be happy to hear it!! Thx

Here's something thats been helping allot. Use MCP's whenever you can. Building my game in unreal with Claude connected through UE5.8 MCP. I'm able to allow claude do every step, from writing code, to building my UI elements, to visually seeing whats on screen, and it does a pretty good job with good direction.

replies.author: Worried-Radish-5316
replies.body: Wow, thank you so much for the suggestion! I’ve been considering Unreal Engine for the rebuild, but I haven’t experimented with its MCP integration yet. I’ll definitely look into the UE5.8 MCP workflow.
